key_insight: BISECT reduces spectral starvation in continual LoRA learning by dividing a fixed low-rank budget between shared invariant features and task-specific novelty.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support sequential adaptation of engineering vision models without storing past examples or adding inference overhead, though solid-mechanics applications are not evaluated.
method: Extract invariant directions from dominant modes of the joint historical-and-current Gram matrix.
Build an orthogonal novelty complement using generalized Rayleigh whitening and complement projection.
Fold trained updates into the frozen backbone, gating invariant atoms by current-to-joint Rayleigh ratios and preserving novelty atoms at unit gain.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that historical null tails capture only 5.5% of incoming-task variance and that BISECT outperforms prompt, adapter, and LoRA baselines across eight incremental settings on five vision datasets.
watch_item: Sensitivity to the invariant–novelty rank split and the computational cost of spectral decomposition are not quantified in the abstract.
paper_title: BISECT: Bilevel Spectral Decomposition for Low-Rank Continual Learning
